audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL (EIP-7951 secp256r1 precompile, EIP-7939 CLZ opcode) and CL (Fulu fork choice with PeerDAS data availability, EIP-7917 deterministic proposer lookahead) logic and their interfaces.

out_of_scope_reasons.JSON-RPC API: Vulnerabilities requiring the user to have publicly exposed an API are explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Fusaka Bug Bounty
out_of_scope_reasons.Beacon API: Vulnerabilities requiring the user to have publicly exposed an API are explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Fusaka Bug Bounty
out_of_scope_reasons.Infrastructure bugs: Webpages, DNS, email, etc. are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.ERC-20 contract bugs: Typically not included per Ethereum Bug Bounty
out_of_scope_reasons.ENS bugs: Maintained by the ENS foundation, not in scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Configuration errors: Requires node operator error, not external attack
out_of_scope_reasons.High-effort DoS: Sustained, CPU or bandwidth intensive, and/or requires more than 1 packet or on-chain transaction
out_of_scope_reasons.Tests and scripts: Cannot be exploited when the client is running

el_vectors.entry_point: On-chain Transaction (e.g., contract calling precompile at 0x100 or executing CLZ opcode)
el_vectors.threat: Submit crafted transactions invoking secp256r1 precompile with malformed inputs to cause incorrect verification results, or exploit CLZ edge cases. Resource exhaustion via precompile spam if gas cost is insufficient.
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks containing transactions with malicious precompile calls or CLZ opcodes.

cl_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with unavailable data to exploit PeerDAS data availability checks. Attempt effective balance grinding to manipulate proposer lookahead schedule. Submit conflicting attestations.
Provide forged or incomplete column sidecars to disrupt data availability verification. Selectively withhold sidecars to cause targeted nodes to reject valid blocks.

cl_vectors.entry_point: External APIs (e.g., MEV-Boost relay, checkpoint sync endpoint)
cl_vectors.threat: Provide incorrect data, censorship, denial of service.

misclassified_entities.reason: A calling smart contract executes within the EVM, which is internal to the EL. The calldata it provides to the precompile originates from on-chain transaction inputs (ultimately from an external user/contract deployer), so the trust boundary is at the transaction submission level. Reclassified as internal relay of untrusted data.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via On-chain Transaction (secp256r1 precompile)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: On-chain transaction calling precompile at address 0x100 with arbitrary calldata
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit a transaction that calls the secp256r1 precompile with arbitrary 160-byte input. All input must be fully validated: length check, signature bounds (0 < r,s < n), public key bounds (0 <= qx,qy < p), curve membership, and non-identity point check. The precompile is reachable via any smart contract CALL/STATICCALL.

trusted_external_entities.name: WebAuthn/FIDO2 Device (signature source)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Signature data relayed through smart contract to secp256r1 precompile
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External hardware devices generate secp256r1 signatures that are relayed on-chain. The device itself is not directly connected to the EL; its data flows through user transactions. The precompile must treat all signature data as untrusted regardless of claimed origin.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer (beacon blocks)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and gossip arbitrary SignedBeaconBlock messages. All blocks must pass full validation pipeline: parent known, slot not future, after finalized slot, finalized ancestry, data availability, and state transition.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer (column sidecars)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Column sidecars are fetched from unauthenticated P2P peers for PeerDAS data availability sampling. Peers may provide forged, malformed, or incomplete sidecars. Each sidecar must be verified for structural integrity (verify_data_column_sidecar) and cryptographic validity (verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs).

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator (proposer grinding)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network: validator operations (effective balance manipulation, RANDAO observation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: A validator may attempt to manipulate their effective balance after observing RANDAO reveals to influence proposer selection. EIP-7917 mitigates this by computing proposer lookahead using effective balances frozen at earlier epochs, but the attack vector exists at the P2P/consensus boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Network (RANDAO reveals)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon block proposals containing RANDAO reveals
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RANDAO values are revealed publicly in block proposals. Any observer can see them. The security of proposer lookahead depends on RANDAO being unpredictable MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD+1 epochs in advance. This is a public, unauthenticated data source.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via On-chain Transaction (CLZ opcode)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: On-chain transaction executing contract containing CLZ (0x1e) opcode
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can deploy and call contracts containing the CLZ opcode. The opcode itself has minimal attack surface (pop 1, push 1, fixed gas), but must handle the zero-input edge case correctly (return 256). Gas cost of 5 must be sufficient to prevent DoS.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full input validation required: (1) input length exactly 160 bytes, (2) signature components 0 < r,s < n, (3) public key coordinates 0 <= qx,qy < p, (4) point on curve qy^2 ≡ qx^3 + ax + b (mod p), (5) point not at infinity. Gas (6900) must be charged before any processing. Invalid inputs return empty output without revert.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Calldata to secp256r1 precompile via smart contract relay
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Device-originated signatures are relayed through untrusted on-chain transactions. No trust in signature origin; all cryptographic validation must be performed by the precompile. Signature malleability (both (r,s) and (r,n-s) valid) is not prevented by the precompile; applications must handle this.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: on_block handler in fork choice store
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: parent root in store, slot not in future, slot after finalized epoch, block descends from finalized checkpoint, data availability confirmed (all column sidecars retrieved and KZG-verified), full state transition execution. Any assertion failure causes rejection.

All column sidecars must be verified for structural integrity (verify_data_column_sidecar) and cryptographic validity (verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs). Sidecars from peers are completely untrusted. Unavailable sidecars cause block rejection or queueing. Time-bounded availability window: MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Proposer lookahead computation at epoch boundary (process_epoch)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Effective balances used for proposer selection must be frozen at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1, before RANDAO for the target epoch is known. Proposer lookahead is computed and stored immutably in beacon state. Post-RANDAO effective balance changes must not affect already-computed schedules.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: RANDAO mix used as seed in proposer lookahead computation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: RANDAO values must be unpredictable MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD+1 epochs in advance. The seed used for proposer selection is derived from RANDAO at epoch - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1. If RANDAO is predictable further ahead, the effective-balance-freezing defense is weakened.

Standard EVM stack validation (underflow check). Fixed gas cost of 5 must be deducted. Input is a single 256-bit stack value (no external data parsing). Zero input must return 256. Execution must be constant-time to prevent timing side channels.
